E-INVOICING · FREE · NO ACCOUNT

Create an XRechnung or Peppol e-invoice

Germany already requires businesses to receive structured e-invoices, and sending becomes mandatory from 2027 (2028 for smaller firms); Belgium, Poland and France follow. A PDF is no longer enough. Fill in the form, get a UBL or CII XML file, and see it checked against the preflight rules before you download it. Totals and the per-rate VAT breakdown are worked out for you. Nothing is uploaded.

Document

Seller (you)

Buyer

Payment

Lines

DescriptionQtyUnitUnit price (net)VAT %VAT categoryExemption reason

0% needs a category: Z zero-rated, E exempt (e.g. Kleinunternehmer § 19 UStG), AE reverse charge, K intra-EU supply, G export, O outside scope. All but Z need a reason.


  


  

    
Want to check an invoice you received or exported from your ERP? Use the E-invoice Preflight checker. Self-hosting an API? See the README in the repository.

    
No warranty. Provided free and as-is. Not legal, tax or accounting advice, not a certified invoicing system, and it neither signs, archives nor transmits invoices. It does not look up Leitweg-IDs or Peppol participants. Review the output and use your network's own validator before relying on it. To the maximum extent permitted by law, the authors accept no liability for any loss arising from its use.

    
Everything runs in your browser; invoice contents are never uploaded and there are no accounts, cookies or analytics vendors. Optional anonymous local counters record only the event name and day. 

    
Free and open source (MIT). If it saved you an invoicing tool subscription, GitHub Sponsors is optional and never changes what the tool does.

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<!--
  A clean UN/CEFACT CrossIndustryInvoice — the syntax used by XRechnung CII and
  by the XML embedded in a Factur-X / ZUGFeRD PDF. This one is a reverse-charge
  supply (VAT category AE), which is the case where a zero rate is correct and
  an exemption reason is expected.

  Line 1   10 x 25.00  = 250.00   AE 0%
  Tax basis              250.00
  VAT                      0.00
  Grand total            250.00
-->

      <udt:DateTimeString format="102">20260824</udt:DateTimeString>
    </ram:IssueDateTime>
  </rsm:ExchangedDocument>

  <rsm:SupplyChainTradeTransaction>
    <ram:IncludedSupplyChainTradeLineItem>
      <ram:AssociatedDocumentLineDocument><ram:LineID>1</ram:LineID></ram:AssociatedDocumentLineDocument>
      <ram:SpecifiedTradeProduct><ram:Name>Software integration hours</ram:Name></ram:SpecifiedTradeProduct>
      <ram:SpecifiedLineTradeAgreement>
        <ram:NetPriceProductTradePrice><ram:ChargeAmount>25.00</ram:ChargeAmount></ram:NetPriceProductTradePrice>

          <ram:LineTotalAmount>250.00</ram:LineTotalAmount>
        </ram:SpecifiedTradeSettlementLineMonetarySummation>
      </ram:SpecifiedLineTradeSettlement>
    </ram:IncludedSupplyChainTradeLineItem>

    <ram:ApplicableHeaderTradeAgreement>
      <ram:BuyerReference>04011000-98765-21</ram:BuyerReference>
      <ram:SellerTradeParty>
        <ram:Name>Supplier GmbH</ram:Name>

        <ram:SpecifiedTaxRegistration><ram:ID schemeID="VA">FR40303265045</ram:ID></ram:SpecifiedTaxRegistration>
      </ram:BuyerTradeParty>
    </ram:ApplicableHeaderTradeAgreement>

    <ram:ApplicableHeaderTradeDelivery/>

    <ram:ApplicableHeaderTradeSettlement>
      <ram:InvoiceCurrencyCode>EUR</ram:InvoiceCurrencyCode>
      <ram:PaymentReference>INV-2026-0043</ram:PaymentReference>
      <ram:SpecifiedTradeSettlementPaymentMeans>
        <ram:TypeCode>58</ram:TypeCode>

how-do-you-calculate-a-mixed-vat-rate-ta.text:
← E-invoice Preflight

How do you calculate a mixed-VAT-rate tax breakdown?

When an invoice has lines taxed at more than one rate, each rate needs its own row: the net of only the lines at that rate, and the tax that net produces at that rate. The table below is the exact fixture the checker's own test suite uses to confirm rule INV-037/INV-038 pass a correct breakdown.

Two lines, two rates

2 × €100.00 consulting at 19%, plus 1 × €100.00 books at 7%. Each line's net is quantity × unit price; each line's tax is that net × its own rate, rounded to the nearest cent.
LineQty × priceRateNetTax
Consulting2 × €100.0019%€200.00€38.00
Books1 × €100.007%€100.00€7.00
tax_breakdown: one row per rate, summing only the lines at that rate. This is what the checker compares the supplied breakdown against.
tax_percenttaxabletax
19€200.00€38.00
7€100.00€7.00

Per rate: taxable = sum of net for every line at that rate. tax = taxable × rate ÷ 100, rounded half-up to the cent. The invoice totals are the sum across rates: €300.00 net, €45.00 tax, €345.00 gross — not one rate applied to the whole invoice.

A single blended calculation would get this wrong. Applying 19% to the full €300.00 net gives €57.00 tax, €12.00 more than the correct €45.00, because the books line is only taxed at 7%. The checker does not average or infer a rate; it groups lines by their own tax_percent first, and every row in the breakdown has to reconcile to that grouping exactly — a row for a rate no line uses, a missing row for a rate that is used, or a taxable/tax figure that does not match the summed lines each produce their own finding (INV-037 for a missing breakdown on a mixed-rate invoice, INV-038 for a supplied one that does not reconcile).

Open the checker and drop your own invoice to see its breakdown validated line by line. Nothing you drop is uploaded.

This page is arithmetic, not tax or legal advice. It does not determine the correct VAT rate for a line or replace review by a qualified professional.

Common questions

How do you calculate a mixed-VAT-rate tax breakdown?

Group the invoice lines by their tax rate, sum each group's net amount, then multiply that group's net by its rate and round to the nearest cent. Two consulting lines totalling €200.00 net at 19% produce €38.00 tax; one books line of €100.00 net at 7% produces €7.00 tax. Each rate gets its own row: 19% / €200.00 / €38.00 and 7% / €100.00 / €7.00. The invoice total (€345.00 gross) is the sum of every line's net plus every line's tax, not a single blended rate applied once.

What happens if a mixed-rate invoice has no tax breakdown?

The preflight checker flags rule INV-037: an invoice mixes tax rates without a per-rate breakdown. If a tax_breakdown is supplied but a row's taxable or tax amount does not match what the lines at that rate actually sum to, or a row's tax is not its taxable amount times its own percentage, it flags INV-038 instead, naming the exact row and the figure it expected.

Drop a JSON, UBL, CII, or Factur-X PDF invoice or credit note — or paste the JSON shape — and get rule IDs plus a suggested fix for missing fields, totals that do not add up, a credit sent as a commercial invoice, a missing original invoice reference, a prepaid that does not leave the stated amount due, a missing remittance on an IBAN transfer, mixed VAT rates without a per-rate breakdown, a 0% line without an exemption reason, a buyer electronic address that fails its GLN or EAS scheme, an invoice period that is incomplete or ends before it starts, a SEPA payment means without an IBAN, a purchase-order field that repeats the invoice number, a header discount that does not match its percent, payment terms days that do not match the due date, and transposed VAT, IBAN, BIC, or RF values. After using this, you can now review a structured invoice in the browser in seconds, which used to mean running a CLI or waiting for a network rejection. Everything stays on this page.

Invoice to check

Drop .json, .xml, or Factur-X .pdf files here, or choose them.

Up to 50 files, 1 MB each. Multiple files also flag repeated invoice numbers.

Or paste one JSON invoice:

What this checks

The same local rules as the CLI: required fields, ISO dates, currency shape, party identifiers, line arithmetic, totals, optional prepaid versus amount due (INV-028 and INV-029), optional VAT, IBAN, and BIC typo catches (INV-022 through INV-027), remittance matching (INV-030 and INV-031), credit-note document type plus original-invoice reference (INV-032 through INV-034), 0% or exempt lines that omit a tax reason (INV-035 and INV-036), mixed tax rates without a per-rate breakdown (INV-037 and INV-038), and optional buyer or seller electronic addresses (INV-039 through INV-041), and an optional invoice period that is incomplete or ends before it starts (INV-042 and INV-043), optional payment means versus IBAN (INV-044 through INV-046), optional buyer or purchase-order references (INV-047 through INV-049), optional header allowances or charges (INV-050 through INV-052), and optional payment terms days versus due date (INV-053 and INV-054). UBL XML, UN/CEFACT CII, and Factur-X / ZUGFeRD PDFs (the embedded XML) are mapped into that shape. A PDF result says Unwrapped factur-x.xml (CII) from the PDF when the standard attachment was opened; custom attachment names are not shown. UBL mapping includes CreditNote, BillingReference, payee account, branch, PaymentID, PaymentMeansCode, TaxExemptionReason, TaxSubtotal, EndpointID, InvoicePeriod, BuyerReference, OrderReference, invoice-level AllowanceCharge, and PaymentTerms SettlementPeriod DurationMeasure. It is not a Peppol, EN 16931, or tax-law validator and it does not submit anything.

Prefer a pipeline? The same checks run from python3 -m einvoice_preflight invoice.json in this directory.

Common questions

Does this submit an e-invoice?

No. The page only reads files or pasted JSON in your browser and reports observations. It never contacts a tax authority or submission network.

How do I check an e-invoice before submission?

Drop a JSON, UBL, or CII (XRechnung / Factur-X) XML invoice or credit note, a Factur-X / ZUGFeRD / XRechnung PDF with an embedded invoice, or paste the JSON shape. The checker unwraps the PDF in the browser when needed and reports missing fields, date-shape mistakes, a header allowance or charge whose amount does not match its percentage, a purchase-order reference that repeats the invoice number or is a placeholder, payment terms days that do not match the due date, a SEPA or credit-transfer payment means without an IBAN, an invoice period that is incomplete or ends before it starts, totals that do not match the line items, mixed tax rates without a per-rate breakdown, a buyer electronic address that fails its GLN or EAS scheme, a credit sent as a commercial invoice, a missing original-invoice reference, a 0% or exempt line without a tax reason, prepaid versus amount-due mismatches, a missing remittance on an IBAN invoice, and optional VAT, IBAN, BIC, and RF typo catches, with a rule ID and a suggested fix. It does not decide tax treatment or legal validity.

How do you calculate a mixed-VAT-rate tax breakdown?

Group the lines by rate, sum each rate's net, multiply by that rate, and round to the cent — see the worked example the INV-037/INV-038 checks are built from.

Every rule this checker reports has an INV- code naming one specific defect and the field it was found in — the rule reference lists all of them with a fix for each. They are this tool's own identifiers, not EN 16931 BR- rules or a submission network's rejection codes.

← E-invoice Preflight

This checker vs. Avalara

Two different shapes: Avalara is an ongoing cloud platform for calculating and filing tax, plus e-invoicing, across a business's whole operation. This page is a free, local, no-account check of one invoice file's fields and arithmetic before it goes anywhere near a submission network.

What each tool is for

Avalara is a cloud-based tax-compliance platform founded in 2004. It automates the end-to-end indirect-tax lifecycle — sales and use tax calculation, returns filing, exemption certificate management, VAT/GST across many countries, and e-invoicing — and integrates with ERP, accounting, and ecommerce systems most businesses already run. It is sold as an ongoing subscription account. Avalara's own current pricing is not reachable from this session to confirm today's plan names or dollar figures, so no price for it is invented here: only its well-documented identity and category — a cloud tax-compliance platform sold as a subscription account — are stated, and no dollar amount for Avalara appears on this page.

This checker does none of what Avalara does. It does not calculate tax owed, file a return, manage exemption certificates, or transmit anything to a tax authority or exchange network. It reads one invoice file — JSON, UBL XML, UN/CEFACT CII (XRechnung CII / Factur-X), or a Factur-X / ZUGFeRD / XRechnung PDF — either dropped into the browser or piped through the CLI, and reports the specific fields, VAT arithmetic, IBAN/BIC/RF digits, or payment instructions that would fail, each with a rule ID and a suggested fix, plus a downloadable remediation CSV. It runs free, keeps no account, and uploads nothing you drop or paste — the browser page never contacts a server. It is a preflight observation, not a declaration that an invoice is legally valid or ready to submit.

QuestionWhere to answer it

Which exact field, total, or VAT digit is wrong, and what is the fix?This checker's rule IDs (INV-001 through INV-054) and its rule reference.
I need exemption-certificate management or a compliance network integration into my ERP.Avalara, or a comparable platform.
How is a mixed-VAT-rate tax breakdown actually calculated?This checker's own worked example.
Do I need to create an account or sign up to use the tool?This checker: no. Avalara is used through a subscription account.

Most teams get different value from each: Avalara (or a comparable platform) for calculating and filing tax and routing e-invoices across an entire operation as an ongoing subscription, and a free local checker like this one for an instant, no-login answer to whether one specific invoice file is well-formed before it reaches that pipeline. Should I use this checker or Avalara?

They do different jobs, and a business that files real returns will likely end up using something like Avalara alongside a tool like this one, not instead of it. Avalara is a cloud tax-compliance platform founded in 2004, covering sales and use tax calculation, returns filing, exemption certificate management, VAT/GST, and e-invoicing across many countries, sold as an ongoing subscription account and integrated into ERP, accounting, and ecommerce systems. what-does-this-e-invoice-error-code-mean.text:
← E-invoice Preflight

What does this e-invoice error code mean?

The preflight reports each defect with a rule code, the field it looked at, and a suggested fix, so you can go straight to the value that needs changing. This page is the full reference: every code the checker can emit, what it means, and what to do about it.

First, what these codes are not

INV- codes are this tool's own identifiers for its own checks. They are not EN 16931 BR- business rules, not Peppol validation artefact identifiers, and not the rejection codes a tax authority or submission network sends back. The preflight reads the file in front of it and reports arithmetic and structural observations before you submit; it never contacts a network, and it does not decide tax treatment or legal validity.

That distinction matters in both directions. A network validator may reject a document this tool passes, because it applies country and scheme rules this tool does not implement. It may also accept one this tool flags, because some of these checks are stricter than a network requires — the remittance and reference checks in particular are about getting paid, not about passing validation. When you contact your network or service provider, quote their code, not this one.

Document structure and required fields

The shape checks. These run first, because most later checks need these fields to exist before they can compare anything.
CodeWhat it meansFix
INV-001The document root is not a JSON object, or a required top-level field is missing. The required set is invoice number, issue date, currency, supplier, customer, lines, and totals.Add the named field. The report gives its path, so /totals means the totals object itself is absent.
INV-002The invoice number is empty or is not text.Provide a non-empty invoice number as a string.
INV-003The issue date is not an ISO calendar date. A date that looks right but does not exist, such as a 31st in a 30-day month, fails here too.Use YYYY-MM-DD.
INV-004The currency is not a three-letter uppercase code.Use an ISO-style code such as EUR or GBP.
INV-007The invoice carries no line items.Add at least one line.
INV-008A line is not an object, so its fields cannot be read.Give the line a description, quantity, unit price, and tax percentage.

Parties: supplier, customer, VAT identifiers, electronic addresses

Checks on who the invoice is from and to. The VAT and endpoint checks are typo catches computed from published checksum and format rules — never a registration or directory lookup, because nothing leaves your browser.
CodeWhat it meansFix
INV-005The supplier or customer identifier is missing.Add the party identifier from the source system.
INV-006The supplier or customer name is missing.Add the party name.
INV-022A VAT identifier uses a country prefix the checker does not recognise.Use a published VAT country prefix, or omit vat_id if the value is an internal identifier rather than a VAT number.
INV-023A VAT identifier fails that country's published checksum — almost always a transposed or dropped digit.Correct the digits. This is a checksum test, not a registration lookup: it cannot tell you whether a well-formed number is actually registered.
INV-039A party's electronic address is present but is not an object carrying both a scheme and an id.Provide endpoint.scheme (the EAS code) and endpoint.id, or omit the endpoint entirely.
INV-040A party's electronic address id is empty or is not text.Provide the id as text, or omit the endpoint.
INV-041The electronic address does not match the published shape for the scheme it declares — for example a GLN whose check digit does not compute.Correct the identifier. This is a format check, not a directory lookup.

Lines, totals, and arithmetic

These are the checks that catch the largest share of real defects, because they compare numbers that were produced at different times by different parts of an ERP export. Everything is rounded half-up to cents before comparison.

Arithmetic checks. Where a figure is wrong, the report names the value the checker computed, so you can paste it straight in if the lines are the side you trust.
CodeWhat it meansFix
INV-009A line quantity is not a positive number.Use a positive numeric quantity.
INV-010A line unit price is not a non-negative number.Use a non-negative numeric unit price.
INV-011A line tax percentage is not a valid number.Use the percentage from your authoritative source. The tool never chooses a tax rate for you.
INV-012A line's net is missing, or does not equal quantity × unit price at cent precision.Set the line net to the computed figure the report names, or correct the quantity and unit price.
INV-013The invoice net total is missing or is not a non-negative number.Provide a numeric net total.
INV-014The net total does not match the sum of the lines after header allowances and charges are applied.Set the net total to the computed figure, or correct the lines and adjustments. If this fires alongside INV-050–INV-052, fix the adjustments first.
INV-015The invoice tax total is missing or is not a non-negative number.Provide a numeric tax total.
INV-016The invoice gross total is missing or is not a non-negative number.Provide a numeric gross total.
INV-017Gross does not equal net plus tax.Set gross to the computed figure, or correct whichever of the three totals is wrong.
INV-018The tax total does not match what the line tax percentages add up to.Set the tax total to the computed figure, or correct the line inputs. On an invoice with more than one rate, read the mixed-rate worked example first — per-rate rounding is the usual cause.
INV-019Batch runs only: the same invoice number appears on more than one file in the batch.Use a unique invoice number, or remove the duplicate before submission.

Tax treatment, exemptions, and per-rate breakdown

Tax checks. The tool reports structural facts about the tax you declared; it never decides what rate or exemption applies.
CodeWhat it meansFix
INV-035A 0% or exempt line carries no exemption reason.Add tax_reason or tax_reason_code on the line, or tax_exemption_reason on the invoice — or correct the tax percentage if the line was not meant to be zero-rated.
INV-036An exemption reason field is present but empty or not text.Provide it as text, or omit it if the line is neither 0% nor exempt.
INV-037The invoice mixes tax rates but carries no per-rate tax breakdown.Add tax_breakdown with one row per rate, or use a single rate. The worked example shows the arithmetic this check expects.
INV-038A tax breakdown row is not an object.Give each row a tax percentage, a taxable amount, and a tax amount.

Dates, invoice periods, and payment terms

Date checks. Impossible orderings are caught here — an end before a start, a due date before issue — because receiving systems commonly reject them outright.
CodeWhat it meansFix
INV-020The due date is not an ISO calendar date.Use YYYY-MM-DD.
INV-021The due date is earlier than the issue date.Set the due date to the issue date or later.
INV-042The invoice period is present but is not an object with both a start and an end.Use period.start and period.end as ISO dates, or omit the period.
INV-043The invoice period ends before it starts.Set the end to the start date or later.
INV-053Payment terms days is empty, or is not a positive whole number of days.Use a positive whole number such as 30, or omit payment.terms_days.
INV-054The due date does not equal the issue date plus the stated terms days. This usually means one of the two was edited by hand and the other was not.Set the due date to the computed date the report names, or correct the terms days.

Payment: IBAN, BIC, means, and remittance

These checks are about getting paid rather than passing validation. A network may well accept an invoice that fails them; a buyer's accounts-payable system may still not be able to pay it.

Payment checks. The IBAN and BIC tests are computed locally from published checksum and country rules — no bank is contacted.
CodeWhat it meansFix
INV-024The payment IBAN is empty or is not text.Provide the IBAN as text, or omit payment.iban.
INV-025The IBAN fails its published country checksum — a transposed digit is the usual cause, and it is the defect most likely to cost you a payment.Correct the digits. This is a checksum test, not a bank lookup: a well-formed IBAN can still be the wrong account.
INV-026The payment BIC is empty or is not text.Provide the BIC as text, or omit payment.bic.
INV-027The BIC's country does not match the IBAN's country.Correct whichever is wrong so both agree, or omit the BIC.
INV-030The invoice names an IBAN but no remittance reference, so a buyer paying it has nothing to quote on the transfer.Add payment.remittance, or omit the IBAN if payment is not by transfer.
INV-031The remittance reference is empty or is not text.Provide it as text, or omit it.
INV-044The payment means code is empty or is not a documented UNCL 4461 code.Use a published code such as 30, 58, or 10, or omit payment.means.
INV-045The means is a credit transfer, SEPA transfer, or direct debit, but no IBAN is given.Add the IBAN, switch to a cash or card means, or omit the means.
INV-046The means is cash, cheque, or card, yet the invoice also names an IBAN — the two disagree about how you expect to be paid.Use a transfer means with the IBAN, or drop the IBAN.

Settlement amounts, document type, and references

Checks on what is still owed, what kind of document this is, and the references a buyer's accounts-payable system matches against.
CodeWhat it meansFix
INV-028The prepaid amount is present but is not a non-negative number.Provide a numeric prepaid amount, or omit totals.prepaid.
INV-029The amount due is present but is not a non-negative number.Provide a numeric amount due, or omit totals.due.
INV-032The document type is not a known invoice, credit note, or debit note.Use invoice, credit_note, or debit_note, or omit the field.
INV-033A credit or debit note does not name the invoice it reverses.Add original_invoice with the number being credited or debited.
INV-034A credit or debit note names itself as the invoice it reverses — usually a template that copied the invoice number into both fields.Point original_invoice at the original document, not at this one.
INV-047The buyer reference is present but empty, not text, or a placeholder.Add the cost-centre or buyer text the buyer asked for, or omit buyer_reference.
INV-048The purchase-order reference is present but empty, not text, or a placeholder.Add the buyer's purchase-order number, or omit order_reference.
INV-049The purchase-order reference repeats the invoice number, which is what an export does when the buyer's PO was never captured. Accounts payable cannot match it.Set it to the buyer's actual purchase-order number, or omit it.

Header allowances and charges

Document-level discounts and surcharges — the ones applied after the lines are summed.
CodeWhat it meansFix
INV-050The adjustments field is present but is empty or is not a list of rows.Provide a list of allowance or charge rows, or omit adjustments.
INV-051An allowance or charge base is missing or invalid, so its amount cannot be checked against its percentage.Provide a non-negative base, or omit both base and percent and state the amount directly.
INV-052An allowance or charge reason is longer than the 100-character field receiving systems commonly provide.Shorten the reason so it survives the receiving system, or drop the row.

Read failures

Reported when the file could not be parsed at all, so no other check could run against it.
CodeWhat it meansFix
INV-READThe invoice could not be read — malformed JSON, XML that is not UBL or CII, or a PDF with no embedded invoice XML to unwrap.Resolve the read error and run the preflight again. For a PDF, confirm it is a Factur-X, ZUGFeRD, or XRechnung file that actually carries an XML attachment.

Common questions

What does an INV rule code from the e-invoice preflight mean?

Each INV code names one specific defect the preflight found in the invoice you gave it, so that a report can point at a single field rather than saying the document is bad. INV-012 means a line's net does not equal quantity times unit price. INV-017 means gross does not equal net plus tax. INV-018 means the tax total does not match what the line tax percentages add up to. INV-025 means an IBAN fails its published country checksum. INV-045 means a credit-transfer or SEPA payment means was given without an IBAN. These are the tool's own identifiers for its own checks, not codes issued by a tax authority or a submission network.

Are these the same codes my e-invoicing network sends back on a rejection?

No. INV codes are internal to this preflight and are not EN 16931 BR- rule identifiers, Peppol validation artefact codes, or any authority's rejection codes. The preflight runs before submission and reports arithmetic and structural observations about the file in front of it. A network's own validator may accept a document this tool flags, or reject one it passes. Use the INV code to find and fix the underlying field; quote your network's code, not this one, when you contact them.

Why did the preflight flag my invoice when the totals look right?

The most common cause is cent rounding applied at a different stage than the checker applies it. The preflight rounds half-up to cents and compares the rounded figures, so a line net carried at full floating precision in an ERP export can disagree with the printed total by a cent and raise INV-012, INV-014 or INV-018. The second most common cause is a field that is present but empty rather than absent — an empty string is not a missing field, and several checks treat the two differently. The report names the JSON path of the value it compared, which is the fastest way to see which of the two it is.
